Q2: What do the sk-create-manual-testing-playbook and sk-create-feature-catalog validators check today, and which of those checks touch the code rather than the document shape?

graphEvents.label: Q1 drift sources and current catchers

label: The playbook validator's only code-touching checks are local-markdown-link resolutions (missing, case mismatch, symlink escape); scenario options, exact command sequences and expected answers are checked for presence and internal prompt sync only, never against code behavior.

The catalog validator's code-touching surface is best-effort path existence only: SOURCE FILES cells and prose tokens resolve only for .skilled/.opencode/.claude/.codex prefixes or doc-relative markdown links, line-range suffixes are stripped before the check so line anchors are never validated, and source-anchor accuracy is left to manual review.

cite-drift-scan.mjs already extracts path:line citations outside fences and covers every tracked .md under .skilled/skills (scenario files and catalog leaves included), classifying past_end and moved targets with zero model calls by default, but no .github workflow invokes it and its per-document form is only an advisory at the end of validate_document.py.

Enforcement is asymmetric and line-window-blind: the playbook contract is a hard CI gate on every PR, push and schedule, the catalog package validator is referenced by no workflow (only its unit tests run in CI), and a citation whose target content moved while staying within the file's line count resolves in_range, so no current check compares a cited line's content to the claim.

validate-doc-model-refs.js is the existing doc-to-code cross-check pattern: it loads canonical model names from code (registry.ts), flags markdown citing non-canonical defaults, and runs report-only in the advisory CI job -- the lightest in-repo shape a playbook or catalog self-check could copy instead of executing the corpus.

Existence and line-bounds checks cannot detect in-range content drift: a citation that still resolves can carry a claim the cited lines no longer support, so any check built solely from path existence or line-count bounds is blind to semantic drift.

The playbook CI gate already treats absence-of-result as failure (it asserts every fail-closed root is still discovered, because a backlog once grew while the corpus scan silently covered a third of the roots), a fail-closed discipline any new drift check should inherit.

Known-context prior drift matches the uncaught class exactly: a scenario and its catalog entry passed --phase-count, an option create.sh never had and accepted silently, and a DOC-331 admission scenario's expected answer disagreed with the router; both are expected-answer drift no current check tests.

direction: Execute each scenario's Exact Command Sequence in CI as the drift check
reason: Command sequences mix agent: steps with operator-dependent state (the REQUIRED_COMMAND_SEQUENCE check accepts prose, including agent: steps), scenarios are manual contracts by design, and the brief's non-goals rule out new runners or heavy machinery; the topic asks for the lightest self-check, which points at static resolution instead.
